title: Point Orders at the New Queue
description:
**SITUATION:**

Orders are not reaching the queue. Last night the queue cluster moved from `queue-old.internal` to `queue.internal`, but **order-processor** is still sending every new order to the old host, which no longer exists. There is no config-management tool on this box, so you change this one file in place.

The file is `/etc/order-processor/app.conf`. Both queue URLs still say `queue-old.internal`. Logging is still `debug`, which will fill the disk. Old `TODO` lines sit next to real settings. Also, `metrics_port = 9100` is written in the config file but commented out, so monitoring of this process cannot be achieved.

One required line is missing. The new cluster will not accept work until the `[queue]` section contains `max_retries = 5`. That line is not in the file yet, so it has to be added. Before any of this, keep an exact copy of the original at `/etc/order-processor/app.conf.bak`.

**YOUR TASK:**

1. Copy the original to `/etc/order-processor/app.conf.bak` before you edit.
2. Replace every `queue-old.internal` with `queue.internal`.
3. Change `log_level` from `debug` to `info`.
4. Delete every line containing `TODO`.
5. Uncomment `metrics_port = 9100`.
6. In `vim`, add `max_retries = 5` inside the `[queue]` section.

**SPEC:**

- `/etc/order-processor/app.conf.bak`: an exact copy of the original
- `url = amqp://queue.internal:5672` and `fallback = amqp://queue.internal:5673`
- the payments `endpoint` line is unchanged from the original
- `log_level = info`, no `TODO` lines, `metrics_port = 9100` with no leading `#`
- `max_retries = 5` is inside `[queue]`; every other line is untouched

**REFERENCES:**

- [DevSetu Blog — Edit: sed for one-line changes](/play/devops-engineer/linux/read/reading-and-searching-text#sed-in-place)
- [DevSetu Blog — Read, Edit and Search Text: less, tail, vi, grep](/play/devops-engineer/linux/read/reading-and-searching-text)

hints: You are learner on a real Ubuntu machine with systemd; sudo works without a password.
Reset gives you a fresh machine (your changes are wiped).
Read SPEC carefully, then Submit — the grader checks the machine itself.
problemStatement.overview: Point Orders at the New Queue
problemStatement.brief: Point Orders at the New Queue
problemStatement.solution:
There is no config-management tool on this box, so you edit `/etc/order-processor/app.conf` yourself. `sed` is for the repeatable changes: the same command would fix a hundred servers. `vim` is for the one new line that is not in the file yet. The file is owned by root, so these commands use `sudo`.

Copy the original first. If an edit goes wrong, the backup is the only copy of what the file used to say.

| Piece | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `sed 's/old/new/g'` | Replaces every match. Without `-i` it only prints the result |
| `sed -i -e ...` | Writes the edits back into the file. Each `-e` is one edit |
| `\.` | A literal dot. A bare `.` matches any character |
| `/TODO/d` | Deletes every line that contains `TODO` |
| `^` | The start of a line, so `#metrics_port` is not matched mid-line |
| `vim` | Opens the file. `o` inserts a line below, `:wq` saves, `:q!` quits without saving |

## 1. Look, then back up

```bash
cat -n /etc/order-processor/app.conf
sudo cp /etc/order-processor/app.conf /etc/order-processor/app.conf.bak
```

## 2. The repeatable edits

Preview the host change before you write it:

```bash
sed 's/queue-old\.internal/queue.internal/g' /etc/order-processor/app.conf
```

Then apply all four edits:

```bash
sudo sed -i \
  -e 's/queue-old\.internal/queue.internal/g' \
  -e 's/^log_level = debug$/log_level = info/' \
  -e '/TODO/d' \
  -e 's/^#metrics_port/metrics_port/' \
  /etc/order-processor/app.conf
```

The first edit replaces both queue URLs. The payments endpoint is `payment.internal`, so this pattern does not touch it.

## 3. Add the line in vim

```bash
sudo vim /etc/order-processor/app.conf
```

1. Type `/\[queue\]` and press Enter to jump to the section.
2. Press `o`, type `max_retries = 5`, then press Esc.
3. Type `:wq` and press Enter.

Check the difference, then **Submit**:

```bash
diff /etc/order-processor/app.conf.bak /etc/order-processor/app.conf
```
